cards.text: Catch-up time, friend. Zechariah, a priest, and his wife Elizabeth are old and never had children, and Zechariah hasn't been able to speak since he didn't believe the angel Gabriel's message (Luke 1:5-7, 1:19-20). Now Elizabeth's time comes, and she gives birth to a SON!

cards.question: When Elizabeth's neighbors and relatives hear that the Lord has shown her great mercy, they rejoice with her.

cards.text: On the eighth day, everybody comes to circumcise the baby, and the crowd already has a name picked out. I don't think anybody asked them for one, but here they are, holding it like a sign at the airport.

cards.question: The crowd is going to name the baby after his ___ Zechariah.

cards.text: Then Elizabeth speaks up about that name. And when the new mom speaks up, friend, the whole room better be listening.

cards.question: Elizabeth agrees to name the baby Zechariah, after his father.
Elizabeth tells the crowd, "No!" Then what does she say the baby shall be called?

cards.text: The relatives push back. Suddenly this baby's name is a group project, and everybody in the room thinks they're the team lead.

cards.question: What's the relatives' problem with the name John?

answers.text: Nobody in the family has that name
The priests already picked a name
Only a king could use that name

cards.text: So they take it to Dad. They make signs to Zechariah to find out what he wants to name the child, and now a room full of grown adults is playing charades with the new father.

cards.question: Zechariah answers the relatives by asking for a ___.
What does Zechariah write on the tablet?

cards.text: Everybody's amazed. The relatives just lost the name vote TWO to NOTHING, and one of those votes came in on a tablet.

cards.question: Immediately Zechariah's mouth is opened and his tongue is released. What does he start doing?

cards.text: All the neighbors are filled with awe. People all through the hill country of Judea are talking about it, and this news is moving faster than a group chat with one juicy update.

cards.question: Everyone who hears about it wonders in their hearts. What do they ask?

answers.text: Where did this child come from

cards.question: The Lord's hand was with this child.

cards.text: Then Zechariah is filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesies. The man who couldn't say ONE word now has a whole message from God, and he is NOT keeping it short.

cards.question: Zechariah begins with "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel," and then gives the reason. What is it?

answers.text: He has visited and redeemed His people
He has rebuilt the temple for His people
He has sent rain on the land of His people

cards.text: Zechariah says God has raised up a horn of salvation for His people. And no, friend, not the kind you lean on in traffic.

cards.question: Zechariah says this horn of salvation is raised up in the house of God's servant ___.
Zechariah says this salvation is brand new, and no prophet ever spoke of it before.

cards.text: It's salvation from their enemies and from all who hate them. God is showing mercy to their fathers and remembering His holy covenant.

cards.question: Zechariah says that covenant goes back to an oath God swore to whom?

cards.text: Deliverance from hostile hands. And listen, friend, God doesn't just rescue His people FROM something. He rescues them FOR something.

cards.question: Zechariah says that once they're delivered, they'll serve God without fear, in holiness and righteousness, all the days of their lives.

cards.text: Then Zechariah turns and speaks right to his baby. A grown man pouring out a prophecy to a newborn, and I bet that newborn slept through the WHOLE thing.

cards.question: Zechariah says his child will be called a ___ of the Most High.
Zechariah says John will go on before the Lord. What will John do for Him?

cards.text: And John's job comes with a message. He'll give God's people the knowledge of salvation.

cards.question: Zechariah says this salvation comes through the forgiveness of their sins.

cards.text: All of this comes from the tender mercy of God. And because of it, Zechariah says, the Dawn will visit from on high.

cards.question: Zechariah says the Dawn will come to shine. Who will it shine on?

answers.text: Those who live in the palace
Those who live by the temple

cards.text: Friend, I spent years in a dark junk drawer, so trust me, the light coming in is the BEST part. And this Dawn doesn't just shine, it guides their feet into the path of peace.

cards.question: As John grows up, he lives in the ___ until the time of his public appearance to Israel.

cards.text: The child grows and becomes strong in spirit. And that's where we'll leave John for now, friend, because this story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: In Luke 1:61 the speakers are only 'They', the people who came for the circumcision in 1:59, which can include the neighbors and relatives of 1:58. The card names them 'The relatives', so it narrows who is speaking. Cards 9, 11 and 13 build on the same narrowing.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer 'tablet' is an object. The wrong answers 'witness' and 'priest' are people, so the right answer stands out by kind.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word inside the line of Zechariah's song ('the house of His servant ___'). Story card 3 gives nothing to reason toward David, so it tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Luke 1:74 gives a purpose ('that we may serve Him without fear'). The card turns it into a statement of sequence and future fact ('once they're delivered, they'll serve God').

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Luke 1:78 says 'because of the tender mercy of our God', and it is tied to the forgiveness in 1:77. The card says 'All of this comes from the tender mercy of God', which widens how the verses connect beyond what the text states.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 18 already covers John living in the wilderness and says 'As John grows up'. Card 19 then steps back to tell the earlier part of Luke 1:80 (the child grows and becomes strong in spirit), so it doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line, 'And that's where we'll leave John for now', nearly copies the doc's example 'And that's where we'll leave it for now' instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
